svg.title: Building a faster Python re: Python reference corrected; full test suite still blocked by 8,244 independently unverified fuzz cases
svg.desc: Pinned Python 3.14.6 remains the baseline. Two genuine Python workers independently confirmed the corrected 6,912-case public-type reference. The complete phase-one correctness oracle is still BLOCKED: all 8,244 seeded supplemental fuzz records have verified checksums, but zero have been rerun through two independent Python reference workers and no replacement has run them. The previous public-type reference remains FALSIFIED. All seven actual gate blockers are preserved. The latest real from-scratch Rust test still has 1,440 proven compatibility differences and 14,853 explicitly verified passes, 512 more differences than historical V7, which had 928 differences and 8,965 verified passes. Its 13 real workers, 13 suite results, six first mismatches and three failure categories remain intact. Six from-scratch candidate families and zero fully compatible replacements are established. The exporter repair remains NOT BUILT and NOT RUN; its build remains SOURCE FROZEN and BLOCKED, with zero compilers, native binaries or candidate workers. Exactly three authenticated phase-one source owners raise the existing evidence and historical-reference lower bounds from 204 / 209 to 207 / 212. Original 31,237 cases, 50 signature checks, 32 public-interface observations, 32 large-input observations and 8,244 supplemental fuzz cases are separately counted. Real 2-GiB candidate checks have NOT RUN. The 4,194,304-case final holdout has not been generated or opened. Speed, memory, confidence intervals and undefined behavior are NOT MEASURED. Runtime independence remains NOT ESTABLISHED.
svg.text: The goal: match Python exactly, then measure whether any from-scratch replacement is actually faster.
